title: Structural Organisation in Animals: Animal Tissues and Frog
syllabus: Animal tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular and Neural tissues; Morphology, anatomy and functions of different systems (digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous, excretory and reproductive) of Frog (Rana tigrina) and Insect brief account.

questions.question: Which of the following types of epithelial tissue forms the inner lining of blood vessels (endothelium) and lung alveoli to facilitate diffusion?
questions.solution: Simple squamous epithelium consists of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. It is found in walls of blood vessels and air sacs (alveoli) of lungs where it forms a diffusion boundary.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding types of Epithelial Tissues and their specific locations in the human body:

List-I (Epithelial Tissue)List-II (Location)
(A) Cuboidal with brush border (microvilli)(I) Inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes
(B) Ciliated epithelium(II) Tubular parts of nephrons (PCT) in kidneys
(C) Columnar epithelium(III) Lining of stomach and intestine
(D) Compound epithelium(IV) Dry surface of skin and buccal cavity

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Simple cuboidal with microvilli: PCT of nephron; Ciliated epithelium: Bronchioles and Fallopian tubes (moves mucus/ova in specific direction); Columnar epithelium: Lining of stomach and intestine (secretion and absorption); Compound epithelium: Dry skin, pharynx, and buccal cavity (protection against chemical and mechanical stresses).

questions.question: Which of the following cell junctions facilitates rapid cell-to-cell communication by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for the transfer of ions, small molecules, and sometimes big molecules?
questions.solution: Gap junctions facilitate communication between neighboring cells by directly connecting their cytoplasm, allowing rapid transfer of ions, second messengers, and small metabolites. Tight junctions prevent leakage across tissues; adhering junctions cement neighboring cells together.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Connective Tissues and their anatomical features:

List-I (Connective Tissue)List-II (Defining Feature / Example)
(A) Areolar tissue(I) Chondrocytes enclosed in lacunae within pliable matrix
(B) Adipose tissue(II) Attaches skeletal muscles to bones (dense regular)
(C) Tendon(III) Loose tissue beneath skin containing fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells
(D) Cartilage(IV) Specialized loose tissue beneath skin for fat storage

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Areolar tissue: Loose sub-epidermal supporting framework containing fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells; Adipose tissue: Fat-storing cells located beneath skin; Tendon: Dense regular collagenous tissue connecting skeletal muscle to bone; Cartilage: Solid, pliable matrix containing chondrocytes in lacunae.

questions.question: Ligaments attach:
options: One bone to another bone (dense regular connective tissue)
questions.solution: Ligaments are dense regular connective tissues consisting of parallel collagen and elastic fibres that attach one bone to another bone at joints.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Muscle Tissues:

List-I (Muscle Type)List-II (Structural Characteristics)
(A) Skeletal muscle(I) Involuntary, non-striated, fusiform/spindle-shaped, uninucleated
(B) Smooth muscle(II) Involuntary, cylindrical, branched, striated with intercalated discs
(C) Cardiac muscle(III) Voluntary, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleated with distinct striations

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Skeletal muscle: Striated, voluntary, cylindrical, multinucleated; Smooth muscle: Involuntary, unstriated, fusiform with single central nucleus (walls of blood vessels, stomach, intestine); Cardiac muscle: Involuntary, striated, branched, uninucleate, possessing communication junctions called intercalated discs.

questions.question: In cardiac muscle tissue, which specialized structures act as communication junctions allowing wave-like synchronous contraction of heart muscle cells as a unit?
questions.solution: Intercalated discs are specialized communication junctions with gap junctions and desmosomes in cardiac muscle fibres that allow electrical depolarization waves to spread rapidly, enabling the myocardium to contract as a functional syncytium.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding neural tissue is INCORRECT?
options: Neuroglial cells make up less than one-fourth of the total volume of neural tissue in the human body.
Neurons are the excitable structural and functional units of neural system.
Neuroglial cells protect and support neurons.
When a neuron is stimulated, an electrical disturbance travels along its plasma membrane.
questions.solution: According to NCERT, neuroglia (supportive non-neuronal cells) make up more than half the volume of neural tissue in our body, not less than one-fourth.

questions.question: In Indian Bullfrog (Rana tigrina), the dorsal surface of the body is olive green with dark irregular spots, while the ventral surface is:
questions.solution: In Rana tigrina, the dorsal skin is olive green with dark irregular spots, whereas the ventral skin is uniformly pale yellow.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the external morphology and sensory organs of a Frog:

List-I (Structure)List-II (Location / Function)
(A) Nictitating membrane(I) Receives sound signals (auditory organ)
(B) Tympanum(II) Protects the eyes while in water
(C) Vocal sacs(III) Webbed appendages for swimming
(D) Hindlimbs(IV) Male sound-amplification organs for croaking

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Nictitating membrane: Transparent third eyelid protecting eye underwater; Tympanum: External eardrum receiving sound vibrations; Vocal sacs: Sound-amplifying pouches in male frogs; Hindlimbs: 5-toed muscular limbs with webbed feet for swimming and leaping.

questions.question: Male frogs can be distinguished from female frogs by the presence of:
options: Vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of forelimbs
Larger body size and red stripes on dorsal skin
questions.solution: Male frogs are distinguished by sound-producing vocal sacs under the throat and a copulatory (nuptial) pad on the ventral surface of the first digit of the forelimbs, which are absent in females.

questions.question: In frogs, food is captured by a specialized tongue which is:
options: Bilobed and attached at the front anterior tip
Trilobed and attached at the back
questions.solution: The tongue of a frog is muscular, sticky, and bilobed, and is attached at the anterior front of the lower jaw, allowing it to be rapidly flipped outward to capture prey.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the digestive system of Frog:

List-I (Organ/Secretor)List-II (Secreted Fluid / Role)
(A) Liver(I) Hydrochloric acid (HCl) and gastric juices
(B) Gall bladder(II) Produces bile
(C) Stomach walls(III) Stores bile juice
(D) Pancreas(IV) Produces pancreatic juice containing digestive enzymes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Liver secretes bile; Gall bladder stores bile; Stomach produces HCl and gastric juices for digesting proteins into chyme; Pancreas secretes enzyme-rich pancreatic juice into the duodenum via the common hepatopancreatic duct.

questions.question: In frogs, respiration on land is accomplished by which of the following three modes?
questions.solution: On land, frogs perform respiration through three routes: (1) Buccopharyngeal respiration via moist oral cavity, (2) Cutaneous respiration through moist, vascular skin, and (3) Pulmonary respiration via a pair of pink sac-like lungs.

questions.question: During aestivation (summer sleep) and hibernation (winter sleep), gaseous exchange in frog takes place EXCLUSIVELY through:
questions.solution: During periods of environmental dormancy (hibernation and aestivation) under mud/soil, frogs suspend pulmonary respiration and breathe solely through their moist, vascular skin (cutaneous respiration).

questions.question: The heart of a frog is a muscular organ enclosed by a double-walled membrane called pericardium. It consists of:
options: Three chambers: two atria and one ventricle
Four chambers: two atria and two ventricles
Two chambers: one atrium and one ventricle
Three chambers: one atrium and two ventricles
questions.solution: The heart of a frog has 3 chambers: two upper atria (right and left) and a single lower thick-walled ventricle. It is covered by a protective double-layered pericardium.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the circulatory structures of Frog:

List-I (Heart/Vessel Structure)List-II (Anatomical Feature)
(A) Sinus venosus(I) Conical sac on ventral side arising from ventricle
(B) Truncus arteriosus(II) Triangular chamber on dorsal side joining right atrium
(C) Hepatic portal system(III) Vascular connection between kidney and lower parts of body
(D) Renal portal system(IV) Vascular connection between liver and intestine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Sinus venosus: Triangular venous chamber receiving vena cavae on dorsal side of right atrium; Truncus arteriosus: Arterial trunk leaving ventral side of single ventricle; Hepatic portal system: Vein network carrying blood from gut to liver; Renal portal system: Venous network from hind legs/lower body to kidneys.

questions.question: The red blood corpuscles (erythrocytes) of a frog are:
questions.solution: Unlike human RBCs (which are enucleated and biconcave), frog erythrocytes are nucleated, oval/biconvex in shape, and contain hemoglobin pigment.

questions.question: The excretory system of a frog consists of a pair of compact, dark red, bean-shaped kidneys located dorsally. Structurally and functionally, adult frog kidneys are composed of:
questions.solution: Each kidney in a frog is composed of thousands of structural and functional filtration units called uriniferous tubules or nephrons.

questions.question: Regarding nitrogenous excretion, an adult frog is ________, whereas its aquatic tadpole larva is ________:
questions.solution: An adult frog excretes urea and is ureotelic, whereas the free-swimming aquatic tadpole larva excretes toxic ammonia directly into water and is ammonotelic.

questions.question: In male frogs, the ureters act as a common urogenital duct because they carry:
options: Both sperms and urine into the cloaca
questions.solution: In male frogs, ureters emerge from kidneys and receive spermatozoa from testes via vasa efferentia and Bidder's canal, functioning as a common urogenital duct that opens into the cloaca. (In females, ureters and oviducts open separately into cloaca).

questions.question: In the male reproductive system of frog, 10 to 12 vasa efferentia arise from the testes, enter the kidneys on their side, and open into:
questions.solution: In male frogs, 10-12 vasa efferentia originate from the testes, enter the medial border of kidneys, and open into Bidder's canal, which communicates with the urogenital duct.

questions.question: A mature female frog can lay approximately how many ova at a single spawning?
questions.solution: A mature female frog lays 2500 to 3000 eggs (ova) at a time during spawning in water.

questions.question: Fertilisation and embryonic development in frogs are respectively:
options: External (in water), Indirect with a tadpole larval stage
Internal, Direct without any larval stage
questions.solution: Fertilisation in frogs is external (taking place in water). Development is indirect, passing through a free-swimming, herbivorous, gill-bearing tadpole larva that undergoes metamorphosis to become an adult frog.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the divisions of the Frog's brain:

List-I (Brain Region)List-II (Constituent Parts)
(A) Forebrain(I) Pair of prominent Optic lobes
(B) Midbrain(II) Cerebellum and Medulla oblongata
(C) Hindbrain(III) Olfactory lobes, paired Cerebral hemispheres, and unpaired Diencephalon

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Forebrain: Olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, unpaired diencephalon; Midbrain: Pair of prominent optic lobes; Hindbrain: Cerebellum and medulla oblongata (which exits via foramen magnum into spinal cord).

questions.question: How many pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain of a frog?
questions.solution: The frog's peripheral nervous system includes 10 pairs of cranial nerves originating from the brain and 10 pairs of spinal nerves originating from the spinal cord.

questions.question: Dense irregular connective tissue with fibroblasts and randomly oriented collagen bundles is predominantly found in:
questions.solution: Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) oriented in various directions and is present in the dermis of the skin.

questions.question: Which of the following cells of areolar tissue secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin involved in inflammatory responses?
questions.solution: Mast cells located in areolar connective tissue synthesize and release bioactive mediators including histamine (vasodilator), serotonin (vasoconstrictor), and heparin (anticoagulant) during inflammation and allergy.

questions.question: The matrix of bone is hard and non-pliable due to the heavy deposition of:
questions.solution: Bones have a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts (hydroxyapatite) and collagen fibres, providing skeletal support and rigidity.

questions.question: Osteocytes (bone cells) reside within small fluid-filled spaces in the hard matrix called:
questions.solution: Osteocytes (mature bone cells) are situated in concentric spaces called lacunae distributed throughout the mineralized bone lamellae.

questions.question: In a frog's digestive system, microvilli and internal folds called rugae in the intestinal wall serve to:
options: Increase the effective surface area for absorption of digested nutrients
questions.solution: The internal mucosa of a frog's small intestine has longitudinal folds (rugae) and numerous microscopic finger-like projections (microvilli) that substantially increase the surface area for nutrient absorption.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the circulatory system of a frog:
Statement I: Frogs have a closed circulatory system with double incomplete circulation.
Statement II: Oxygenated blood from lungs and deoxygenated blood from body mix to some extent in the single ventricle.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Frogs possess a 3-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle) where oxygenated blood from the left atrium and deoxygenated blood from the right atrium enter the single ventricle and partially mix, exhibiting incomplete double circulation.

questions.question: In female frogs, the ovaries are located near the kidneys and have:
options: No functional connection with kidneys, and oviducts open separately into the cloaca
Direct anatomical connection with Bidder's canal
Common opening with ureters inside the renal pelvis
questions.solution: A pair of ovaries is situated near the kidneys, but there is no functional or anatomical connection between the ovaries and the kidneys. A pair of oviducts arising separately from the ovaries opens independently into the cloaca.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the sensory structures of Frog:

List-I (Sense Organ)List-II (Nature / Structure)
(A) Sensory papillae(I) Cellular aggregations on tongue for taste
(B) Taste buds(II) Simple unit organs for touch (tangoreceptors)
(C) Eyes(III) Organs for vision (spherical, simple, located in orbits)
(D) Internal ear(IV) Statoreceptor for hearing and balance

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Sensory papillae: Touch organs (tangoreceptors); Taste buds: Gustatory organs on tongue; Eyes: Simple paired eyes in orbits; Internal ears: Organs of both hearing and equilibrium (statoreceptor).

questions.question: Which of the following endocrine glands is located on the ventral surface of kidneys in a frog as a dark yellow irregular stripe?
questions.solution: Adrenal glands in frogs are found on the ventral surface of both kidneys as prominent, elongated, golden-yellow cortical/medullary strips.

questions.question: The cloaca in frogs is a common terminal chamber that receives:
options: Fecal matter from rectum, urine from ureters, and gametes (sperms/ova)
questions.solution: The cloaca is a small, median, terminal three-way chamber used to pass fecal matter from the rectum, urine from the kidneys/bladder, and gametes (sperms or ova) to the exterior.

questions.question: In a frog's digestive system, partially digested acidic food that leaves the stomach and enters the duodenum is called:
questions.solution: In the stomach, food is ground and mixed with HCl and gastric enzymes into a semi-fluid acidic paste called chyme before passing through the pyloric valve into the duodenum.

questions.question: Which of the following types of glands secrete their products through ducts into the epithelial surface (e.g., mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes)?
questions.solution: Exocrine glands release secretions (mucus, saliva, earwax, digestive enzymes) via tubes or ducts onto the apical epithelial surface. Endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones directly into extracellular fluid/blood.

questions.question: Unicellular glandular epithelial cells scattered among columnar cells of the alimentary canal that secrete protective mucus are:
questions.solution: Goblet cells are isolated, single-celled (unicellular) exocrine glandular cells distributed within the columnar epithelial lining of the gastrointestinal tract that secrete lubricating mucus.

questions.question: Which of the following features is ABSENT in a Frog (Rana tigrina)?
options: Tail and neck in adult stage
questions.solution: The body of an adult frog is divided into only head and trunk; a distinct neck and tail are completely absent in the adult stage.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Cartilage and their anatomical locations:

List-I (Cartilage Type/Location)List-II (Site in Human Body)
(A) Hyaline cartilage(I) Tip of nose and external ear pinna
(B) Elastic cartilage(II) Between adjacent vertebrae in vertebral column
(C) Fibrous cartilage(III) End of long bones, ribs, and larynx

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Hyaline cartilage: Articular ends of long bones, tracheal rings, larynx, rib-sternum junctions; Elastic cartilage: Tip of nose, external ear pinna, epiglottis; Fibrocartilage: Intervertebral discs and pubic symphysis.

questions.question: In frogs, bile juice secreted by the liver and stored in the gall bladder functions to:
options: Emulsify fats and neutralize acidic chyme
questions.solution: Bile emulsifies dietary fats into small droplets and alkalizes the acidic chyme coming from the stomach, facilitating the action of pancreatic lipases.

questions.question: Blood vascular system of frog contains which of the following components?
options: Heart, blood vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries), and blood (plasma, RBCs, WBCs, platelets)
Heart and gills without vascular capillaries
questions.solution: Frogs have a closed, well-developed cardiovascular system consisting of a 3-chambered heart, blood vessels (arterial, venous, capillary systems), lymphatic system (lymph, lymph channels, lymph nodes), and blood composed of plasma and nucleated formed elements.

questions.question: Smooth muscle fibres are described as:
options: Involuntary, non-striated, spindle-shaped with tapering pointed ends
questions.solution: Smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends (fusiform/spindle-shaped), are uninucleated, lack striations, and are under involuntary autonomic control.

questions.question: Frogs are beneficial to human agriculture and ecosystems because they:
options: Eat harmful insect pests protecting crops and maintain ecological balance in food webs
Help in seed dispersal of crops
questions.solution: Frogs are ecologically important carnivores that consume insect pests, preventing crop damage and maintaining balance as critical secondary consumers in wetland and terrestrial food chains.
